subject: body
title: Bones and the Skeleton
about: Goes deeper than Heart, Lungs and Bones: how many bones a grown-up has (206) and why a baby has more, the backbone that bends because it is a stack, the long leg bones, kneecap and jaw, 27 bones in one hand and 12 pairs of ribs, bones that are alive and make new blood in their marrow, how a cast lets a broken bone mend, the X-ray, sunshine and vitamin D, and two fun facts (the smallest bone is in the ear, the funny bone is a nerve). Inside-the-body anatomy is a bridge topic beyond NC Grade 1; the closest codes are 1.NPA.1.2 (foods and why we eat them), 1.NPA.2.1 and PE.1.HF.3.2 (activity that builds a strong body). Read it together: the tablet reads every card aloud while he feels each bone on himself.
tip: Have him feel his own backbone, kneecap and jaw as each card comes up, and bend his elbow to find the joint.

cards.q: How many bones does a grown-up have?
cards.note: Two hundred six bones, from the big thigh bone to the tiny bones inside your ears.

cards.q: A baby is born with about 300 bones, but a grown-up has 206. Where did the extra bones go?
cards.note: Many baby bones are soft and in pieces. As you grow, the pieces harden and join into one bigger bone.

cards.q: Feel the bumpy row of bones down the middle of your back. What is it called?
cards.note: The backbone is also called the spine. It holds you up straight and protects the nerves inside it.

cards.q: Your backbone is a stack of many small bones instead of one long bone. Why is that good?
cards.note: One stiff bone could not curl. A stack of little bones bends forward, back and side to side.

cards.q: The longest and strongest bone in your body is in your...?
cards.note: It is the thigh bone, from your hip to your knee. Your arms and legs are full of long, strong bones.

cards.q: Are your bones dry sticks, or are they alive and growing?
cards.note: Bones are living parts of you, with blood flowing to them. They grow longer and thicker until you are grown.

cards.q: Deep inside your big bones is a soft, jelly-like part. What does it make?
cards.note: That soft part is called bone marrow. It makes new blood cells every second of the day.

cards.q: A bone breaks. What does the doctor put on it while it heals?
cards.note: A cast holds the bone still so the two ends can grow back together. Most casts come off in a few weeks.

cards.q: Wiggle your fingers. About how many small bones are in just one hand?
cards.note: Twenty seven bones in each hand, with long thin ones in your fingers. That is why hands can do so much.

cards.q: The round bone in front of your knee is your...?
cards.note: The kneecap is a little shield for your knee joint. Knee pads cover it when you skate or ride.

cards.q: Which bone moves up and down when you chew and talk?
cards.note: The lower jaw is the only big bone in your head that moves. Your teeth sit in your jaws.

cards.q: Playing outside in the sun helps your skin make vitamin D. What does vitamin D help you build?
cards.note: Vitamin D helps bones soak up calcium from milk and food. Eggs, fish and milk have vitamin D too.

cards.q: The smallest bone in your body is inside your...?
cards.note: It is called the stirrup and is about the size of a grain of rice. It helps you hear.

cards.q: You bump your elbow and it tingles. People call that the funny bone. What is it really?
cards.note: A nerve runs right past your elbow bone. Bump it and the nerve sends a buzzy, tingly message.

cards.q: What kind of picture lets a doctor see the bones inside you?
cards.note: An X-ray camera takes a picture right through your skin. Bones show up white.

cards.q: Feel the ribs on the sides of your chest. How many pairs of ribs do you have?
cards.note: Twelve pairs, twenty four ribs in all. They join the backbone behind and the breastbone in front.
